subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: For Anthropic setup-token and manual-token auth, should OpenClaw physically sync portable static token credentials to sibling agent stores, rely on main-store inheritance, or only add validation and guidance?
rationale: The implementation choice changes where sensitive provider credentials live and prior linked PRs showed that a broad sync helper can accidentally propagate OAuth refresh material.

options.title: Sync static tokens only
options.body: Copy only portable static token credentials for the intended setup-token/manual-token flows, add readback validation and tests, and keep OAuth copying opt-in via the existing portability policy.

options.title: Use inheritance only
options.body: Keep runtime main-store inheritance as the sharing mechanism and improve prompts, status, doctor, and docs so users understand that sibling files do not need physical copies.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Improve the Claude setup-token instructions and post-write validation but leave multi-agent propagation unresolved for now.

recommendation.title: Sync static tokens only
recommendation.body: Copy only portable static token credentials for the intended setup-token/manual-token flows, add readback validation and tests, and keep OAuth copying opt-in via the existing portability policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history across setup-token restoration, Claude CLI preference, and the auth read-through behavior that defines the security boundary.
